about.title: Avenal Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Avenal's economy relies on agricultural operations, warehousing, and the businesses that support Kings County's working population, and injuries on these job sites are common enough that most workers eventually encounter the claims process firsthand. California generally treats workers' compensation as the exclusive path against your employer, no matter who was at fault, but that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to what happened to you, a separate third-party claim may be available alongside your workers' comp benefits. Timing matters here — you generally have 30 days to report the injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney familiar with how these overlapping claims work in Kings County, so you understand your options before time runs short.

items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer in California, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be held separately accountable.

items.title: Deadlines Don't Wait
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and a third-party injury claim carries its own 2-year filing deadline, so acting early matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or pursue a claim, and an independent attorney can help you understand your protections.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site in Avenal — do I file a lawsuit or a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault, so that's typically where you start. However, if a third party — like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer — contributed to your injury, a separate claim against them may also be possible. An independent attorney can help sort out which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury in Avenal?
items.answer: No. California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a workers' compensation claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, it's worth discussing your situation with an independent attorney as soon as possible.
